bib.title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models

read.skipped: References skimmed; appendix figure panels and MultiRC examples are text-only samples.

question: Are there subquadratic operators that can match the quality of attention at scale?
hypothesis: Three properties of attention (data control, sublinear parameter scaling, unrestricted context), distilled from reasoning tasks, explain the quality gap, so an operator with all three but subquadratic cost can close it.
contributions: Hyena operator: recurrence of implicitly parametrized long convolutions and element-wise gating, O(N L log L)
Extended mechanistic-interpretability style synthetic benchmark suite (associative recall, majority, counting, ICL of functions, arithmetic) used to compare long-convolution parametrizations
Language modeling at sub-billion scale reaching GPT perplexity with 20% fewer FLOPs at seq 2K, no attention
Runtime benchmark: crossover with FlashAttention between 4096 and 8196, 100x at 64K
Drop-in replacement for attention in ViT

method.summary: Hyena replaces attention with N+1 input projections, a short depthwise conv on the projections, filters generated by a shallow sine-activated FFN on a positional encoding times an exponential-decay window, and N rounds of FFT long convolution followed by gating. Models are trained from scratch as GPT-style language models on WikiText103 and The Pile (125M to 355M, preliminary 1.3B) with standard GPT hyperparameters, and compared with GPT, RWKV and GPTNeo, plus synthetic tasks and ViT.

results.claim: Hyena solves associative recall at 131k tokens (vocab 30) while Transformer variants do not fit in memory and other attention-free operators fail.
results.setup: 2-layer width-64 models, 2000 training samples, vocab 30, sequence length 131072; order-2 Hyena vs GSS, H3, AFT-conv, RWKV, GPT with FlashAttention (Table 4.2).

results.claim: Among long-convolution parametrizations inside order-2 Hyena, FFN-based implicit filters beat CKConv by 80 points at length 131072.
results.setup: Associative recall, seq 131072, vocab 30, 2 layers width 64; Table A.2 CKConv 14.3, TransferFunc 0.5, H3 0.6, FNO 0.3, Conv1d 0.5.
results.quote: with Hyena outperforming CKConv by 80 points.

results.claim: Hyena matches GPT perplexity on The Pile with fewer training FLOPs at 355M.
results.metric: reduction in total training FLOPs at equal perplexity
results.setup: The Pile, GPT2 tokenizer, 355M models, 15B-token run; Table 4.4 FLOPs (1e19): GPT 4.77 vs Hyena-2 3.93 (about 18% by table arithmetic).
results.note: Footnote 9: FLOP reduction is the non-parametric FLOPs of self-attention; depends on D/L ratio. Table 4.4 gives 4.77 vs 3.93 (x1e19), which is about 17.6%, not exactly 20%. At 125M scale FLOPs are equal (1.88 vs 1.87).
results.quote: Hyena is the ﬁrst attention-free, convolution architecture to match GPT quality with a 20%9 reduction in total FLOPs.

results.claim: Perplexity on The Pile at 355M, 15B tokens: Hyena-2 close to GPT, slightly worse.
results.setup: The Pile, 355M, 15B tokens, seq len 2024 (as printed), batch 256.

results.claim: At 125M/153M on The Pile 15B tokens, Hyena-2 (153M) is 11.1 vs GPT (125M) 11.2.
results.setup: The Pile, 15B tokens; Hyena-2 has 153M params vs GPT 125M, so parameter counts differ.

results.claim: On WikiText103, Hyena-3 (125M) ties the Transformer; the slim variant is slightly better.
results.setup: WikiText103, 125M models, GPT2 tokenizer (vocab 50257). Hyena-3 12 layers; slim 18 layers with FFN width multiplier 2.

results.claim: Hyena runtime speedup versus FlashAttention reaches 100x at sequence length 64K.
results.setup: Order-2 Hyena operator with fused CUDA FFTConv kernel, batch size 64, runtime in ms; crossover with attention at 2048, with FlashAttention between 4096 and 8196.
results.note: Abstract says twice as fast as highly optimized attention at 8K and 100x at 64K; intro says 5x over dense attention and 2x over FlashAttention at 8192, and 100x over FlashAttention at 64k where standard PyTorch attention runs out of memory.
results.quote: Hyena speedups reach 100× at sequence length 64K.

results.claim: Hyena is 2x faster than FlashAttention at length 8K.
results.setup: Intro benchmark claim; Hyena speedup at 8192.
results.quote: We measure 5x speedups over dense self-attention at length 8192 – 2x over highly optimized FlashAttention2

results.claim: Hyena (153M, 137B tokens) averages 41.5 zero-shot on SuperGLUE, versus GPTNeo 43.8 and RWKV 40.2, with less than half the tokens of RWKV.
results.setup: SuperGLUE zero-shot via Arora et al. 2022 pipeline; GPTNeo 125M (300B tokens), RWKV-v4 169M (332B tokens), Hyena 153M (137B tokens).

results.claim: Few-shot (3) SuperGLUE average: Hyena 49.3 vs GPTNeo 49.1 and RWKV 43.0.
results.setup: Same models as zero-shot; 3 shots.

results.claim: Hyena-ViT matches ViT on ImageNet-1k at 16x16 patches.
results.setup: ImageNet-1k from scratch, 300 epochs, ViT-B 87M vs Hyena-ViT 88M, 8 A100 GPUs.

results.claim: At 8x8 patches Hyena-ViT is slightly below ViT.
results.setup: ImageNet-1k, seq len 1024.

results.setup: CIFAR-10 2D, 4 residual blocks width 128, 100 epochs, one T4 GPU; 202k vs 268k params; text says 8% speedup and 25% fewer parameters.

limits: Models are sub-billion (355M main; 1.3B only preliminary, 5B tokens, no GPT comparison); authors say 'promising results at the sub-billion parameter scale'.
Speedups only appear at long sequences because Hyena hardware utilization is lower than FlashAttention; crossover 4096-8196.
Pile comparison uses 5-15B tokens; training hyperparameters are standard GPT ones and likely suboptimal for Hyena.

Transformers are only weak on long synthetic recall in a fixed-2000-sample regime; paper concedes they solve it at shorter lengths with enough data, and hybrids with attention give better downstream results up to 8k.
SuperGLUE: Hyena trained 130B (A.2, D.4) or 137B (A.3, Sec 4.3) tokens; zero-shot Hyena average 41.5 is below GPTNeo 43.8; zero-shot scores near chance on several tasks (MultiRC 1.1).
The 20% FLOP reduction counts only non-parametric attention FLOPs and depends on D/L; at 125M the FLOPs are equal.
Preliminary 'scaling law' uses three token budgets at one model size; Pile 355M 15B perplexity is slightly worse than GPT (9.2 vs 9.1).
Later work (not in the paper) such as long-context and larger attention-free models has dated the sub-billion results.

terms.definition: recurrence z^{n+1}_t = x^n_t (h^n * z^n)_t, y = z^{N+1}, with N implicit long convolution filters and N+1 projections
operator encoding a linear transformation u -> y that is nonlinearly defined by u
filter h_t = gamma_theta(t), a parametric function of time step with parameters independent of filter length
